title: Your Virtual Receptionist: Every Call, Demo, Invoice and CRM Update

how_it_works: Retell answers your line in English or Spanish and hands each call to this workflow.
Usually 2-7 calls a day is one every 1 to 4 hours: every one is answered on the first ring, after hours too.
Questions about your excavators, skid steers and forklifts are answered from your inventory list, read live.
It books the in-person look or demo at your facility and texts the caller the time and your address.
You fill a short form after a sale and QuickBooks emails the invoice; every call lands in your CRM with an English note.
setup: Your post does not name your CRM, invoicing tool, phone system or inventory source: shown here as HubSpot, QuickBooks, call forwarding and a Google Sheet. I point each step at yours.
Shown with sample calls. Nothing is on your number until we test it together in English and Spanish.
Your business line forwards to the Retell number only after you sign off.
Texts need a one-time carrier registration first; calls and bookings work while it clears.
I set it up and run it for you on a monthly retainer: prompts, inventory changes and fixes.
need_from_you: Your inventory list: stock number, machine, year, hours, price and status.
Your demo hours and your facility address.
Which CRM and invoicing software you use today, and a login for each.
What only you answer: price offers, financing, trade-ins, delivery.

sections.label: 1 - ANSWER EVERY CALL ABOUT YOUR MACHINES
sections.note: Usually 2-7 calls a day means one every 1 to 4 hours, so a full-time seat mostly waits by the phone. Retell answers every call on the first ring, after hours too, and greets returning callers by name in English or Spanish.

sections.label: 2 - ANSWER THEIR QUESTIONS FROM YOUR INVENTORY
sections.note: Every answer about your excavators, skid steers and forklifts comes from your inventory list, read live on each question. A machine or a detail that is not on the list gets a callback from you, never a guess.

sections.label: 3 - SCHEDULE THE LOOK OR DEMO AT YOUR FACILITY
sections.note: The point of every call: get them to your facility to take a look or see a demo in person. It books the time on your calendar and texts them the machine, the time and your address in their language.

sections.label: 4 - SEND THE INVOICE
sections.note: After a sale you fill a short form from your phone and QuickBooks emails the invoice from your company. Nothing is invoiced until you say who bought which machine and for how much.

sections.label: 5 - UPDATE THE CRM
sections.note: After every call your CRM gets the caller, the machine they asked about and the next step, written in English even when the call was in Spanish. It is keyed on the caller's phone, so a repeat caller never becomes a duplicate.

sections.label: 6 - IF A STEP FAILS, YOU HEAR ABOUT IT
sections.note: One alert covers every step: you get the step that broke and a link to the run, so no caller falls through.

nodes.label: 4 - Caller Asks About a Machine
5 - Read Your Inventory List, Live
6 - Answer From Your Inventory Only, in Their Language
nodes.notes: A machine sold this morning is never offered this afternoon, and a question the list cannot answer gets a callback, not a guess.

params.system_message: You are the phone receptionist for a heavy equipment dealership in New Jersey that sells excavators, skid steers, forklifts and other machines. A caller is on the line right now and Retell will read your answer out loud, so write it the way a person talks on the phone: two to four short sentences, no lists, no symbols, numbers said naturally (about eighteen hundred sixty hours, fifty-two thousand nine hundred dollars). Answer only from the inventory rows you are given (stock_no, type, year, make_model, hours, features, price, status). Never offer a machine whose status is Sold or On Hold as available: say so and offer the closest Available machine of the same type. Quote the listed price only; never discount, negotiate, or promise delivery, financing, trade-in values, warranties or attachments that are not in the row. If the rows do not answer the question, or the caller asks for a machine you do not have, say the sales team will call them back with that, and do not guess. Answer in Spanish when language is es or the question is in Spanish, otherwise in English. End by offering a time to come take a look or see a demo of the machine in person at the facility.

params.system_message: You update the CRM for a heavy equipment dealership in New Jersey after each phone call its AI receptionist handles. The dealership sells excavators, skid steers, forklifts and other machines, and buyers come to the facility to take a look or see a demo in person. Read the transcript and return only what the caller actually said: first and last name, company, email if given, the machine or type they asked about (with the stock number if one was mentioned), what they need it for, their budget if they gave one, whether a look or demo was booked and when, and the next step for the sales team. Set call_type to buyer, selling_a_machine, vendor, spam or other. Set needs_callback to true, with the reason, when the caller asked something the receptionist could not answer (financing, trade-in, price offer, delivery). Write crm_note in English in three short sentences even when the call was in Spanish, and set language to es or en. If something was not said on the call, return an empty string; never guess a name, price or date. Do not use double quotes inside any field.
